entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
John William (Johann Wilhelm), born on June 7, 1562, in Cleves, was the last Duke of Jülich-Cleves-Berg, ruling from 1592 until his death on March 25, 1609. His reign, largely marked by severe mental illness that rendered him incapable of effective governance, precipitated one of the most significant succession crises of the early 17th century in Western Europe. The strategic location of his vast territories, which encompassed the Duchies of Jülich, Cleves, and Berg, and the Counties of Mark and Ravensberg, made their inheritance a flashpoint for the major Catholic and Protestant powers of the Holy Roman Empire and beyond, including the Habsburgs, Spain, France, and the Dutch Republic.

From a young age, John William was educated in Catholicism at the University of Dillingen, a Counter-Reformation stronghold. Upon his father William "the Rich's" death in 1592, he inherited a complex religious landscape, with a largely Protestant populace under a Catholic ruler. His personal struggles with a progressive mental illness, possibly schizophrenia, began even before his accession and worsened dramatically over time, leading to periods of profound delusion and violent outbursts. This incapacitation meant that various regency councils, often fractured by internal disputes and external pressures, administered the duchies, failing to establish a clear succession plan or consolidate power in the face of escalating international interest.
